params.question: Which combination of features should raise clinical suspicion that a patient's skin disease is HIV-related?

answers.text: Lesions that are painful, pruritic, and recurrent

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pain and itch are common in many dermatoses. The HIV-specific triad is about extent, atypicality, and treatment resistance — not symptom character.

answers.text: Lesions that are extensive, atypical in presentation, and refractory to standard treatment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. These three features — wider spread than expected, unusual morphology or distribution, and poor response to standard therapy — are the hallmarks of HIV-modified skin disease.

answers.text: Lesions that are bilateral, symmetric, and well-demarcated

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Symmetry and sharp borders describe many non-HIV conditions such as psoriasis or eczema. The HIV red flags focus on extent, atypicality, and treatment resistance.

answers.text: Lesions that are localised, acute in onset, and self-limiting

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Self-limiting localised disease is the opposite of the HIV pattern. HIV-related dermatoses tend to spread widely and persist despite treatment.

overallFeedback.feedback: The three red flags are: extensive (spreading beyond the usual sites), atypical (unusual morphology or distribution), and refractory (poor response to standard treatment). This triad should trigger HIV testing.
Exactly right. Whenever a familiar skin condition is more extensive, more atypical, or more refractory than expected — especially in a young adult — think HIV and order a CD4 count with serology.

interactions.label: A 30-year-old HIV-positive man presents with white, corrugated plaques on the la

params.question: A 30-year-old HIV-positive man presents with white, corrugated plaques on the lateral border of the tongue that cannot be scraped off with a tongue depressor. What is the most likely diagnosis?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Candidal thrush produces removable white plaques — wiping reveals an erythematous base. The inability to scrape off the lesion rules this out.

Correct. Oral hairy leukoplakia is driven by Epstein-Barr virus and characteristically forms white, corrugated (hair-like) plaques on the lateral tongue that cannot be scraped off — the key feature distinguishing it from thrush.
Oral lichen planus typically shows a lacy, reticular (Wickham striae) pattern on the buccal mucosa, not corrugated plaques on the lateral tongue.
Oral SCC usually presents as an indurated ulcer or mass, not corrugated white plaques, and is far less common in this age group.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key distinguishing feature here is that the plaque cannot be scraped off. Candidal thrush is removable; oral hairy leukoplakia (EBV-driven) is not. Location on the lateral tongue and corrugated texture confirm OHL.

Well done. The combination of lateral tongue location, corrugated texture, and non-removability is pathognomonic for oral hairy leukoplakia — an important mucocutaneous marker of HIV-related immunosuppression.

interactions.label: An HIV-positive patient with a CD4 count of 80 cells/µL presents with multiple v

params.question: An HIV-positive patient with a CD4 count of 80 cells/µL presents with multiple violaceous nodules on the legs and oral mucosa. Which investigation is definitive for distinguishing Kaposi sarcoma from bacillary angiomatosis?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The CD4 count confirms immunosuppression severity but cannot differentiate between these vascular lesions — both KS and BA occur at low CD4 counts.
KOH mount is used to identify fungal elements (pseudohyphae for Candida, septate hyphae for dermatophytes). It has no role in distinguishing vascular lesions.

Correct. Skin biopsy is the definitive investigation because KS (HHV-8–driven vascular neoplasm), BA (Bartonella infection), and pyogenic granuloma (reactive vascular overgrowth) are clinically indistinguishable but histologically distinct.
Tzanck smear detects multinucleated giant cells in herpesvirus infections. It is not useful for vascular lesions like KS or BA.

overallFeedback.feedback: When violaceous vascular lesions appear at low CD4 counts, KS, BA, and pyogenic granuloma can look identical clinically. Skin biopsy with histopathology is the only definitive way to distinguish them — critical because BA is curable with antibiotics.
Exactly. This distinction matters enormously because BA is curable with antibiotics while KS requires chemotherapy — a biopsy is essential before committing to a treatment path.

interactions.label: Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) is a drug allergy to antiretr

params.question: Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) is a drug allergy to antiretroviral therapy that requires stopping the offending medication.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: IRIS is not a drug allergy. It is an inflammatory flare driven by the recovering immune system reacting to pre-existing infections such as herpes zoster or mycobacteria. The timing (weeks after starting ART) can mimic a drug reaction, but the mechanism and management differ — ART should be continued.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — IRIS is not a drug allergy. It occurs when the recovering immune system mounts an inflammatory flare against pre-existing infections (e.g. herpes zoster, mycobacterial disease). Unlike SJS/TEN or DRESS, IRIS does not require stopping ART.

interactions.label: A patient carrying the HLA-B*57:01 allele is started on abacavir and develops fe

params.question: A patient carrying the HLA-B*57:01 allele is started on abacavir and develops fever, rash, and gastrointestinal symptoms within the first week. What is the most important management step?

answers.text: Continue abacavir with antihistamine and steroid cover

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Continuing abacavir in a patient with confirmed HLA-B*57:01–associated hypersensitivity is dangerous. The reaction will escalate, and rechallenge after any interruption can be fatal.

answers.text: Reduce the dose of abacavir by half and monitor closely

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Dose reduction does not prevent progression of abacavir hypersensitivity. This is an immunologically mediated reaction — even small doses can sustain or worsen it.

Correct. In HLA-B*57:01–positive patients, abacavir hypersensitivity is a systemic reaction involving fever, rash, and GI or respiratory symptoms. Rechallenge can cause a severe, potentially fatal reaction — the drug must be stopped permanently.

answers.text: Switch to nevirapine, which has a lower hypersensitivity risk

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Nevirapine is actually the ART drug most commonly associated with SJS/TEN and DRESS. It would be an inappropriate substitute in this clinical scenario.

overallFeedback.feedback: Abacavir hypersensitivity in HLA-B*57:01–positive patients is a systemic immunological reaction. The drug must be permanently discontinued and the patient must never be rechallenged — re-exposure can trigger a severe, life-threatening reaction.

Well done. The HLA-B*57:01 screening test exists precisely to prevent this scenario. Once hypersensitivity occurs, permanent discontinuation without rechallenge is the rule — rechallenge can be fatal.

interactions.label: A patient on nevirapine develops widespread blistering with a positive Nikolsky

params.question: A patient on nevirapine develops widespread blistering with a positive Nikolsky sign. Examination reveals epidermal detachment over 22% of the body surface area. How is this classified?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: SJS is defined by epidermal detachment affecting less than 10% of BSA. At 22%, this has progressed beyond SJS.

Correct. SJS–TEN overlap is defined by epidermal detachment involving 10–30% of the body surface area. This is a continuous spectrum — the same pathological process, classified by extent of skin involvement.
TEN is classified when epidermal detachment exceeds 30% of BSA. At 22%, this falls in the SJS–TEN overlap zone (10–30%).
DRESS presents with fever, facial oedema, lymphadenopathy, eosinophilia, and organ involvement — not primarily with epidermal detachment. The BSA-based classification applies to the SJS–TEN spectrum.

overallFeedback.feedback: The SJS–TEN spectrum is classified by BSA of epidermal detachment: SJS <10%, overlap 10–30%, TEN >30%. At 22%, this patient falls in the overlap zone. Remember, these are not separate diseases but points on a continuum of increasing severity.

Exactly. SJS (<10%), SJS–TEN overlap (10–30%), and TEN (>30%) form a continuous spectrum classified purely by BSA of epidermal detachment. A positive Nikolsky sign is a red flag for ongoing detachment.
